requirements_summary:
Europa Insurance (EMEA insurer) is evaluating Redwood for regulated customer-facing assistant + internal claims workflows. Procurement requires purchasing via GCP Marketplace. Key decision drivers are EU data residency, retention controls, auditability, and a clean shared responsibility model.

Workloads:
- Claims summarization and adjuster copilot (chat + long-context summarization)
- Policy/document search (embeddings + reranking)
- Contact center assistant (streaming chat)

Performance/scale notes (est.):
- P95 latency target for chat: <2.5s to first token, stable streaming; doc search P95 <400ms for embeddings/rerank in-region
- Peak concurrency spikes during weather events; wants predictable throughput option (Dedicated) but prefers Private/VPC for regulated data
- Cost sensitivity: medium; prioritizes predictable spend + ability to cap/route workloads by policy

Security/compliance requirements:
- EU-only processing and storage; strong preference for GCP EU regions (Frankfurt/Netherlands) and explicit data residency statement
- Retention: default short retention, with configurable retention controls; wants ability to set log retention and request deletion workflow
- Audit logs: admin + API + key events; export to existing SIEM (Splunk) via supported mechanisms
- Encryption: at rest and in transit; KMS/CMEK discussion required for Private/VPC; needs clear language for marketplace security review
- Identity: SSO/SAML required for console access; role-based access controls for org/projects

Procurement/packaging:
- "Marketplace first" requirement; wants confirmation of how Redwood org provisioning/entitlements work from GCP Marketplace subscription
- Interested in compliance add-on language (audit log retention, evidence pointers) for internal security questionnaire acceleration
internal_notes:
Shorthand notes from calls/emails:
- Procurement: "We can only transact via GCP Marketplace for net-new vendors this half." (legal won’t sign direct MSA unless marketplace path fails)
- Security: wants explicit statement of where prompts/outputs are processed + whether any data is used for training (answer: no training on customer data by default; confirm wording matches published security overview)
- Residency: they will reject any solution that can fail over outside EU without explicit customer control. Need to align routing/fallback policy language carefully.
- Retention: request for a table: data types (prompts, outputs, embeddings, logs, audit logs) with default retention + configurability.
- Ask: include support SLA language suitable for marketplace listing + an escalation path for entitlement delays.
- SE view: best fit is Redwood Private (VPC) with dedicated capacity in EU region; keep Hosted API as non-prod option. Ensure marketplace SKU mapping supports that narrative.
